messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. They want:

1. In New York: libraries with Reading Room and Fiction section.
2. In Los Angeles: libraries with Wi-Fi and Children Section.
3. In Chicago: libraries with Cafe and Reading Room.

We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities. The function expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities argument is typed as a single value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." The type is "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

It seems the function expects a single facility or an array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates an array of strings? But the union includes "Cafe"[] meaning an array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Maybe they want to pass an array of facilities? The type is ambiguous. But we can guess that we should pass an array of strings representing the facilities we want. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby({location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]}).

So we can pass facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] for New York. For Los Angeles: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]. For Chicago: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

Let's do that.
